column1: primary_source
Basic Law of Governance of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia (1992), art. 1.

Basic Law of the Federal Republic of Germany / Grundgesetz für die Bundesrepublik Deutschland [Basic Law for the Federal Republic of Germany] (1949), Preamble (“Im Bewußtsein seiner Verantwortung vor Gott und den Menschen…” — “Conscious of their responsibility before God and men…”), arts. 1, 20 and 79(3) (the last withdrawing arts. 1 and 20 from amendment — the ‘eternity clause’, Ewigkeitsklausel).
Basic Laws of the State of Israel: Human Dignity and Liberty (1992); Israel — the Nation-State of the Jewish People (2018); Harari Resolution (1950).
Constitution Act, 1982 (Canada), s. 35 and Part V.
Constitution of the Arab Republic of Egypt (2014), arts. 2 and 3.
Constitution of Australia (Commonwealth of Australia Constitution Act 1900), s. 128.

Constitution of the Plurinational State of Bolivia (2009), Preamble and art. 8 (inscribing the ethical-moral principles of the plural society, among them ama qhilla, ama llulla, ama suwa — ‘do not be lazy, do not lie, do not steal’ (Quechua) — and suma qamaña — ‘living well’ (Aymara)).
Constitution of the Federative Republic of Brazil (1988), art. 60, §4.
Constitution of the People’s Republic of China (1982, as amended 2018), Preamble.
Political Constitution of Colombia (1991), art. 7.
Constitution of the Republic of Ecuador (2008), art. 71 (conferring rights on nature, “la naturaleza o Pacha Mama” — ‘nature or Mother Earth’).
Constitution of the Federal Democratic Republic of Ethiopia (1995), Preamble, arts. 8 and 39.
Constitution of the French Republic (1958), arts. 1 and 89.
Constitution of India (1950), Preamble, arts. 17, 44 and 368.
Constitution of the Islamic Republic of Iran (1979), arts. 4 and 13.
Constitution of Ireland / Bunreacht na hÉireann [Basic Law of Ireland] (1937), Preamble.
Constitution of the Italian Republic (1947), art. 139.
Constitution of Japan (1946), arts. 9 and 96.
Constitution of Kenya (2010), arts. 2, 10, 11 and 159.
Political Constitution of the United Mexican States (1917; amendments of 2012 and 2016), arts. 2, 40 and 135.
Constitution of the Republic of South Africa (1996), Preamble, art. 1 and s. 74; interim Constitution (1993), postamble.
Constitution of the Republic of Turkey (1982), arts. 2 and 4.
Constitution of the Russian Federation (1993), arts. 16, 64, 68 and 135; Law of Amendment of the Constitution of 14 March 2020.
Constitution of the Union of Soviet Socialist Republics (1936).
Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria (1999), ss. 10 and 275-284.
Constitution of the Portuguese Republic (1976), art. 288.
Constitution of the Czech Republic (1992), art. 9(2).
Treaty on European Union and Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union; European Convention on Human Rights (1950); Charter of the United Nations (1945), art. 103.
ILO Convention No. 169 concerning Indigenous and Tribal Peoples (1989).
Constitution of the United States of America (1787), Preamble and art. V.
Federal Constitution of the Swiss Confederation (1999), Preamble (“Au nom de Dieu Tout-Puissant!” / “Im Namen Gottes des Allmächtigen!” — “In the name of Almighty God!”).

Treaty of Waitangi / te Tiriti o Waitangi [the Treaty of Waitangi] (1840), English and Māori texts (the two versions differ on the key terms kāwanatanga, ‘governance’, and tino rangatiratanga, ‘full chieftainship/sovereignty’).

Déclaration des droits de l’homme et du citoyen [Declaration of the Rights of Man and of the Citizen] (1789), art. 16 (“Toute société dans laquelle la garantie des droits n’est pas assurée, ni la séparation des pouvoirs déterminée, n’a point de constitution” — “Any society in which the guarantee of rights is not secured, nor the separation of powers determined, has no constitution at all”).
